limits: A rating is ★ coaching over ◆ inputs; the score never gates. The floor (bracket_report.json) is the only bracket gate.
calibrate.py refuses a verdict below 10 decks with 20 games each; no figure here is checked against outcomes yet (`rating --calibrate` reports the refusal with today's n).
Goldfish kill is one column, never the rule: the benchmark is an unopposed ceiling with no blockers and no removal, and a combo or control deck reads slow for not attacking.
Forge is not a power read until the harness work is done (the pilot's rule, 2026-10-18): its component ships at weight 0.00 and is shown only for a run on the current list.
DeckCheck's Threat Index is shown in `context` and never scored.
Diagnostic engine figures are read against each deck's own declaration and are never ranked across decks; they are evidence for the argument, not a component.
rank over n=3 decks; no significance claim

findings.note: rating --json re-run: components, withheld, code_score 73.2, bracket, limits identical to rating.json.
skeleton:speed kill_by_turn_8 is the real speed input (0.774, n=10000).
3 wins in 7 games matches log.jsonl: wins 002, 006, 007; losses 001, 003, 004, 005.

Log 004 quote is verbatim and is the pilot's own account of the loss. The argument uses it as a pattern (optics), and the entry's summary says its sha is backfilled, so the argument correctly attributes nothing to a version.
Log 007 'turn six or seven' is verbatim; the sha 99419d5b equals the current decklist_sha256, so it is the one current-list game.
'Leave this deck alone.' is verbatim, the pilot's closing line.
Quote verbatim; the argument labels it the pilot's unverified arithmetic, which is what the 007 debrief flags and files as a resolve-stack open question. Not over-read.

stack 002 title verbatim; validate-stack says contract holds, checker: pass. It proves Panharmonicon doubling Miirym on a Lathliss entering, and the argument limits the claim to 'that one doubling line'.

68 vs code 73.2 is a modest downward move. The only figures that argue for lower (mana placement 0.0 at missed_land_drop_rate 0.2436, two mana-screw/drought losses) are already scored in mana and construction and the argument says so; figures for higher (kill_by_turn_8 0.774, speed 100, game 007) are already in speed. The table record's Wilson CI [0.158, 0.750] spans par, so neither direction has a named figure beating the stated hedge. No too-generous or too-harsh case I can name.

No unrecorded claims found: 'no pilot-feel survey', 'no Forge run on this list', 'only game 007 on the current list' all match withheld[] and the log shas. No superlatives or rankings over the bracket group; the argument ranks nothing.
Not answered by the artifacts: stacks/ has no Whelp scenario (002 has no cast trigger); resolve-stack can settle it.
Needs more current-list games; only 'rate' can answer, and the skeleton cannot yet.

resolution: the interval spans 0 grade boundaries; measured components carry their inputs' intervals, the judgment none

judgment.argument: The measured components cannot see how a seated table treats this deck. There is no pilot-feel survey and no Forge run on this list, and the goldfish speed score is an unopposed ceiling with no opponents to react. The table record of 3 wins in 7 games is already scored, but it mostly describes older lists; only game 007 was played on the current list. Colour and land count are scored in mana and construction, so I do not mark the deck down for them again. What the scores do not weigh is the shape of the record. The pilot's account of game 004 is "the table converged, and three players picked me apart inside one rotation": a deck that looks fast on paper and gets punished for showing it. Game 007 went the other way. The pilot says "I think I won on turn six or seven" and "Leave this deck alone." It is one game, and its closing count is the pilot's own arithmetic and unverified: "three Whelps with doubled triggers — six, twelve damage every time I cast a dragon". What is verified is narrower: stack 002, "Miirym under Panharmonicon: how many copies?", proves that one doubling line. I hold 68, a little under the measured score: one current-list game carries the upside, and the record shows both a table that converged on the pilot and one that did not.
